object_description: transparent bridge-like volume with a one- to two-storey base and a closed load-bearing upper floor
geometry_property: extends to the neighbouring roof edge
takes up the whole property length
design_condition: the volume extends directly to the rear facade of the sports hall up to its roof edge, taking up the full length of the property so the programme is organised in a transparent base under a closed upper floor

positive: The programme is organised in a transparent volume with a one- to two-storey base and a closed upper floor
The volume stretches like a bridge from the flanking access cores over the vehicle hall
It is closed off with a fire wall towards the street
The uses are cleverly arranged so an attractive address is created with a two-storey window front
This openness is not perceived as disturbing inside
The magazine rooms are clearly on the top closed floor, which serves as static support structure
The architectural implementation is logical and consistent
A modern industrial building of concrete, steel and glass appropriately complements the ensemble
The three usable floors are accessed laterally via two entrances and can be flexibly divided
The proximity of the archive entrance to the park where most visitors come is particularly appreciated
Setting up all vehicles next to each other allows the right vehicle type to be chosen as required
The very beautiful supporting structure has a decisive influence and seems very clear at first glance
The different floors are spatially precisely defined
The view from the mezzanine into the vehicle hall is unique
The cubature is relatively small and yet very cost-effective
The appeal of the project lies in the simple concept
It works as a contemporary interpretation of the commercial building
A compact volume with good functional processes and an attractive openness suits the public character
negative: The reading of the volumes and the consequences of the extension are questioned
Extending to the roof edge creates a building conglomeration rather unfamiliar to the area
It also brings interior disadvantages, with doubts that the height can be maintained given tight room heights
Converting storage into offices would only be possible with skylights or atriums
The work area behind the cars is more limited than with double parking
The structure requires very large spans and the load-bearing box is very challenging
The floor width is too large to be supported by the side walls alone
The central wall is not high enough to carry the loads and the vertical supports are insufficient
The alignment requirement no longer allows the central wall height to be corrected
Without an additional support row the lateral projection of the mezzanine ceiling is too large
That additional support row would significantly obscure the ground floor and mezzanine
No energy and building technology concept is explained
Decentral technology centres are not ideal for maintenance
The high proportion of glass on ground floor and mezzanine is rated critical for the energy balance
Doubts about the urban approach, the static feat and the limited space and room heights prevail
The strength of the structural proposal is therefore also its weakness
